items.example: Don't worry about the tickets, it's all sorted.
items.exampleTr: Biletleri dert etme, her şey ayarlandı.
items.simple: Everything is done and fixed. No problem now.
dialogue: A: Did you book the taxi for tomorrow?
B: Yep, sorted.
items.note: İngiliz argosu; tek başına 'Sorted!' = Tamamdır!

items.example: I was gobsmacked when she said she was moving to Australia.
items.exampleTr: Avustralya'ya taşınacağını söyleyince ağzım açık kaldı.
items.simple: So surprised that your mouth falls open.
dialogue: A: They're getting married after two weeks?
B: I know, I was gobsmacked.
items.note: İngiliz argosu; 'gob' = ağız.

items.example: Stop faffing about and get in the car!
items.exampleTr: Oyalanmayı bırak da arabaya bin!
items.simple: Waste time doing small, silly things instead of the main job.
dialogue: A: Are you ready yet?
B: Nearly, I'm just having a faff with my hair.
items.note: İngiliz argosu; isim olarak 'What a faff!' = Ne zahmet!

items.example: That jumper's a bit naff, isn't it?
items.exampleTr: O kazak biraz zevksiz, değil mi?
items.simple: Cheap-looking and not cool.
dialogue: A: Do you like the decorations?
B: Honestly? They're a bit naff.
items.note: İngiliz argosu; Amerikanca yakın karşılığı 'cheesy' ya da 'tacky'.

items.example: You won again? You jammy thing!
items.exampleTr: Yine mi kazandın? Ne şanslı şeysin!
items.simple: Very lucky, maybe more lucky than fair.
dialogue: A: I found twenty quid on the pavement!
B: You jammy so-and-so.
items.note: İngiliz argosu; kıskançlıkla karışık takılma.

items.example: His parents are loaded, so he's never had a job.
items.exampleTr: Ailesi çok zengin, o yüzden hiç çalışmadı.
items.simple: Having lots and lots of money.
dialogue: A: Did you see her new car?
B: Yeah, she must be loaded.
items.note: Hem İngiliz hem Amerikan argosu; İngilizcede 'minted' da denir.

items.example: Half the class skived off on Friday.
items.exampleTr: Sınıfın yarısı cuma günü okulu ekti.
items.simple: Stay away from school or work when you should be there.
dialogue: A: Where's Dan?
B: I think he decided to skive today.
items.note: İngiliz argosu, genelde 'skive off'; Amerikanca 'play hooky'.

items.example: The driving test was a doddle.
items.exampleTr: Sürüş sınavı çocuk oyuncağıydı.
items.simple: Something very, very easy.
dialogue: A: Is the new software hard to use?
B: No, it's a doddle.
items.note: İngiliz argosu; Amerikanca 'a breeze', 'a cinch'.

items.example: Are you taking the mickey out of my accent?
items.exampleTr: Aksanımla dalga mı geçiyorsun?
items.simple: Laugh at someone or tease them, sometimes unkindly.
dialogue: A: Nice hat. Very... brave.
B: Don't take the mickey!
items.note: İngiliz argosu; 'take the mick' da denir. Ayrıca 'fazla ileri gitmek'.

items.example: He threw a sickie to watch the match.
items.exampleTr: Maçı izlemek için yalandan rapor aldı.
items.simple: Say you are ill so you can skip work, but you are not.
dialogue: A: The weather's amazing today.
B: Don't even think about it. You can't throw a sickie again.
items.note: İngiliz ve Avustralya argosu; Amerikanca 'call in sick' (dürüst olmasa da).

items.example: We had a good chinwag over coffee.
items.exampleTr: Kahve eşliğinde güzel bir muhabbet ettik.
items.simple: A long, friendly chat.
dialogue: A: Where have you been for an hour?
B: Just having a chinwag with the neighbour.
items.note: İngiliz argosu, sıcak ve şakacı.

items.example: There was a bit of a kerfuffle at the checkout.
items.exampleTr: Kasada biraz curcuna çıktı.
items.simple: A small fuss or noisy mix-up.
dialogue: A: What was all the shouting about?
B: Just a kerfuffle over a parking space.
items.note: İngiliz İngilizcesi; büyük olmayan karışıklıklar için esprili kelime.

items.example: I had a dodgy kebab last night and I've felt sick all day.
items.exampleTr: Dün akşam şüpheli bir kebap yedim, bütün gün midem bulandı.
items.simple: Not safe, not honest, or not working well.
dialogue: A: He's selling iPhones for fifty quid.
B: Sounds dodgy to me.
items.note: İngiliz argosu; kişi, yemek, araba, diz için. Amerikanca 'sketchy'.

items.example: Some bloke at the pub bought us a drink.
items.exampleTr: Bardaki adamın biri bize içki ısmarladı.
items.simple: A man, any ordinary man.
dialogue: A: Who's that talking to your mum?
B: Just a bloke from her book club.
items.note: İngiliz argosu; Amerikanca 'guy'. Kadın için kullanılmaz.

items.example: I'm so bummed the concert got cancelled.
items.exampleTr: Konserin iptal olmasına çok bozuldum.
items.simple: Sad and disappointed.
dialogue: A: Did you get the tickets?
B: No, they sold out. I'm bummed.
items.note: Amerikan argosu; İngilizcede 'gutted'a yakın.

items.example: Don't count on Mark, he's really flaky.
items.exampleTr: Mark'a güvenme, son anda ekmeyi çok sever.
items.simple: A person who makes plans but often doesn't show up.
dialogue: A: She cancelled on me again.
B: She's always been flaky.
items.note: Amerikan argosu, İngiltere'de de yaygın; 'flake' = sürekli ekip giden kişi.

items.example: That new sushi place is a bit spendy.
items.exampleTr: O yeni suşi yeri biraz tuzlu.
items.simple: It costs a lot of money.
dialogue: A: Should we go to that rooftop bar?
B: Sure, but it's kind of spendy.
items.note: Amerikan argosu (özellikle batı yakası); 'pricey'nin argo hali.

items.example: I'm beat. I'm going straight to bed.
items.exampleTr: Bittim. Doğruca yatağa gidiyorum.
items.simple: I am very, very tired.
dialogue: A: Want to watch another episode?
B: No, I'm beat.
items.note: Amerikan argosu; İngilizcede 'knackered'.

items.example: That part of town gets a bit sketchy at night.
items.exampleTr: Şehrin o kısmı geceleri biraz tekinsiz oluyor.
items.simple: It feels not safe or not honest.
dialogue: A: The website wants my passport number.
B: That's sketchy. Don't do it.
items.note: Amerikan argosu; İngiltere'de 'dodgy'. Ayrıca 'eksik, belirsiz' bilgi için.

items.example: Is this offer legit or is it a scam?
items.exampleTr: Bu teklif gerçek mi yoksa dolandırıcılık mı?
items.simple: Real and honest, not fake. Also: really.
dialogue: A: This burger is legit the best I've ever had.
B: Told you!
items.note: Amerikan kökenli, gençler arasında her yerde; 'legit amazing' = harbiden harika.

items.example: He's still salty about losing the game.
items.exampleTr: Maçı kaybettiği için hâlâ kıl.
items.simple: Upset and bitter about something small.
dialogue: A: Why won't Ozan talk to me?
B: He's salty you beat him at FIFA.
items.note: Amerikan ve internet argosu; gençler arasında yaygın.

items.tr: kapış! benim! (bir şeye ilk hak iddia etmek)
items.example: Dibs on the front seat!
items.exampleTr: Ön koltuk benim!
items.simple: You say it fast to be the first to get something.
dialogue: A: Who wants the last slice?
B: Dibs!
items.note: Amerikan argosu; 'call dibs on something'. İngilizcede 'bagsy'.

items.example: After the flight, I was completely zonked.
items.exampleTr: Uçuştan sonra tamamen bitkindim.
items.simple: So tired that you could fall asleep anywhere.
dialogue: A: Where's Grandpa?
B: Zonked on the sofa after lunch.
items.note: Amerikan argosu; 'zonk out' = sızıp kalmak.

items.example: They bought a house way out in the boonies.
items.exampleTr: Ta dağ başında bir ev almışlar.
items.simple: A place very far from towns and shops.
dialogue: A: Where does your cousin live?
B: Out in the boonies. No phone signal at all.
items.note: Amerikan argosu; 'boondocks'un kısası. İngilizcede 'the middle of nowhere'.
